original_question: Let f(n) be the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. Does the lower asymptotic normalized gap satisfy lim inf_{n→∞} (f(n) − n)/√n ≤ √3?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Conjecture 1.5 (Lai [30]): determine whether lim inf_{n→∞} (f(n) − n)/√n ≤ √3, where f(n) is defined at the start of Section 1 as the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. refined_question: Let f(n) denote the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices such that no two cycles in the graph have the same length. Is it true that lim inf_{n→∞} (f(n) − n)/√n ≤ √3?
justification: The draft is targeting the exact weaker conjecture stated in Section 1 as Conjecture 1.5. The nearby context first defines f(n), then records the upper bound of Theorem 1.2 and the lower bound of Theorem 1.3, then states Conjecture 1.4 and immediately says that it would be nice to prove one of the following weaker conjectures, the first of which is precisely Conjecture 1.5 with the inequality lim inf_{n→∞} (f(n) − n)/√n ≤ √3. So the right refinement is to keep the question essentially as written, while making it explicit that this is the paper’s Conjecture 1.5 and keeping the scope on f(n) rather than nearby variants such as f2(n).
